newsitem.title: UK: Poll shows Britons want Charles to marry Camilla.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Britons want Charles to marry Camilla.

text.p: British public opinion has turned full circle in the past year and is now in favour of heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles marrying his lover Camilla Parker Bowles, Thursday's Daily Mirror said.
The tabloid said it carried out a poll of 500 people and found 68 percent in favour of Charles marrying Camilla, who celebrates her 50th birthday on Friday.
When Charles was divorced from Princess Diana last year, Camilla was widely blamed for the breakdown of the royal marriage and polls showed deep hostility to the idea that she might marry Charles.
Charles confessed in a 1995 television interview that he had resumed his love affair with Parker Bowles, whom he had known since 1971, when his marriage to Diana had irretrievably broken down.
But in recent months, the media appears to have warmed to Camilla and she has been applauded for her discretion. She has never spoken to the press and has never willingly been photographed.
Although Charles said at the time of his divorce that he did not plan to remarry, he has kept up his relationship with Parker Bowles and will on Thursday throw a lavish party for her birthday.

The Daily Mail newspaper said that Britain's new government is taking so seriously the prospect that Charles and Camilla could marry, that it is drawing up guidelines for what the Mail said could be "potentially the most serious constitutional crisis since the abdication of Edward VIII" in 1936.
